page: Microsoft Azure D48d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 server family. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly with the instance, offering 1843 GB of local SSD capacity. This virtual machine runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the D48d_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. The system achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 46630.34 and a PassMark CPU score of 48327.07. Cryptographic capabilities are a notable strength, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 25% at 42548.75, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets. Memory bandwidth is measured at 152.26 GB/sec for large block reads and 65.92 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-specific tests, the server demonstrated strong image processing capabilities, scoring 14999.0 in Geekbench, and achieved a strong text generation speed of 285.96 tokens/sec during LLM inference with a small 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D48d_v5 offers a balanced resource density, combining substantial compute power with a large local SSD without the premium cost of dedicated memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. However, a key tradeoff is the reliance on standard x86_64 architecture and the absence of specialized AI accelerators, which limits its efficiency for heavy deep learning workloads, as evidenced by a lower text generation speed of 2.81 tokens/sec on a large 70B LLM model. This server is best suited for relational databases, enterprise application hosting, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose business workloads requiring fast local temporary storage.
